Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Summary of current findings
  • Right knee pain with mechanical symptoms (clicking) and exertional onset (~2 weeks ago) during marathon training.
  • Pain begins after ~20 minutes of running (around mile 2–3); improved with rest; transient effusion after first run that resolved with ice; current ROM preserved (can fully straighten and fully flex); no persistent swelling, warmth, or fever.
  • No current instability or locking; intermittent tingling in right toes after runs; prior knee trauma (ice hockey injury) several months ago; uses NSAIDs periodically for joint discomfort; ongoing high activity with running.
  • Management discussed includes continued ice therapy, reduction in running load, NSAIDs with caution, and formal knee examination with physiotherapy assessment; imaging only if persistent or evolving symptoms.
- DDx integration (consistent with transcript)
  • Meniscal tear (traumatic or degenerative) — High likelihood
  • Patellofemoral pain syndrome / chondromalacia patellae — High likelihood
  • Osteoarthritis of the knee (degenerative) — Medium likelihood
  • Iliotibial band syndrome — Medium likelihood
  • Traumatic ligament injury (ACL/MCL) — Low likelihood but to consider given fall on ice
  • Others (e.g., inflammatory arthritis) — Considered but less likely given lack of systemic features
- Noted conflicts
  • No conflicts identified between transcript and DDx; no contradictory data requiring “conflict noted.”

Management Plan
- management_plan_main_or_not_recorded
  • Continue icing knee as currently practiced.
  • Ease up on running volume/intensity; avoid activities that provoke pain.
  • NSAID strategy: continue NSAIDs as tolerated; doctor may prescribe a slightly stronger anti-inflammatory to be used regularly rather than ibuprofen, with dosing appropriate to food intake; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  • Initiate knee examination by physiotherapist for comprehensive assessment and provocative testing.
  • Referral to physiotherapy (long assessment of the knee) with consideration of potential knee imaging (MRI) if indicated after exam.
  • If persistent swelling, warmth, redness, fever, or new locking occurs, seek urgent review.
  • If timing allows and symptoms persist, clinic appointment available if wait times are prolonged.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Meniscal tear (traumatic or degenerative) — High
  • Rationale: Clicking with movement, activity-related knee pain emerging after several minutes of running, prior knee trauma, transient effusion; ROM preserved.
- Patellofemoral pain syndrome / chondromalacia patellae — High
  • Rationale: Pain with knee bending and running, mid-knee location, crepitus noted; common in runners; no systemic symptoms.
- Osteoarthritis of the knee (degenerative) — Moderate
  • Rationale: Age 44–45 with overuse; intermittent discomfort with activity and possible early degenerative changes.
- (If included) Iliotibial band syndrome — Moderate
  • Rationale: Running-related knee pain; typical location is lateral knee; not clearly described in this case.
- (If conflicts arise) Traumatic ligament injuries (ACL/MCL) — Low
  • Rationale: Mechanism of fall on ice; current exam shows no instability or locking; nonetheless remains part of differential until exam.
